This document provides information about the use of the messages for Target2-Securities – Securities Reporting and includes, for example, business transactions and messages flows.
The Message Definition Report (MDR) is made of three parts:

This describes the contextual background required to understand the functionality of the proposed message set. Part 1 is produced by the submitting organization that developed or maintained the message set in line with an MDR Part 1 template provided by the ISO 20022 Registration Authority (RA) on www.iso20022.org.
This is the detailed description of each message definition of the message set. Part 2 is produced by the RA using the model developed by the submitting organization.
This is an extract if the ISO 20022 Business Model describing the business concepts used in the message set. Part 2 is an Excel document produced by the RA.

The main objectives of this document are as follows:
to provide information about the messages that support the business processes

This Message Definition Report covers a set of five MessageDefinitions developed by Banco de España and Banque de France on behalf of 4CB in close collaboration with SWIFT, submitted by Deutsche Bundesbank on behalf of 4CB and approved by Securities Standards Evaluation Groups (SEG) on 19 February 2026.

Originally, these messages have been designed to support the T2S community with retrieving securities settlement and securities position related information from the platform. T2S (TARGET2-Securities) is a European securities settlement engine which offers centralised settlement in central bank money across all European securities markets. The fundamental objective of T2S is to integrate and harmonise the highly fragmented securities settlement infrastructure in Europe. It aims to reduce the costs of cross-border securities settlement and increase competition and choice among providers of post-trading services in Europe.
The detailed description of each MessageDefinition is provided in Message Definition Report Part 2.

The Securities Transaction Penalties report message is specifically designed to support the provision of information to T2S actors related to the cash penalties computed by T2S that are either imposed or credited to those actors or their participants. On a daily basis, T2S shall compute cash penalties for settlement instructions which have not been settled after their intended settlement date.

Additionally, this message also supports the reporting of cash penalties that have been modified since its first calculation in T2S by a CSD or recalculated by T2S due to several circumstances like changes in the penalty rates to be applied or the valuation of the ISIN of the settlement instructions related to the penalty.

These messages are to be used with the ISO 20022 Business Application Header (head.001). The schema and more information about the Business Application Header (BAH) can be found on the www.iso20022.org web site
Settlement Queries Responses Reports message set consists of:
This section provides for an overview of the functionality of each message in the scope of this submission, See Message Definition Report Part 2 for the message definitions and formats.
The Settlement Queries Responses and Report message definitions are specifically designed to support the following technical functions:

The Securities Account Position Query provides CSDs and T2S participants with the functionality to query for the latest or historical data on balances in the Securities Accounts with multiple criteria and, in some cases, satisfying multiple values or range of values.
The Securities Account Position Query message is composed of the following message building blocks.
This building block is mandatory and defines the criteria used to report on the securities account position allowing to choose for the latest or historical data.
This building block is mandatory and provides the criteria to extract the securities account position result set.

In response to the Securities Account Position Query T2S sends a Securities Account Position Response message (semt.040) with the corresponding Securities Account position details matching the criteria as defined within the query.

The Securities Settlement Transaction Query message is sent by a Central Securities Depository or a Directly Connected T2S Participant (e.g. payment bank/settlement bank) to T2S to query for information on securities settlement instructions with multiple criteria and, in some cases, satisfying multiple values or range of values.
This message is composed of the following message building block:
This building block is mandatory and non-repetitive. It contains the definition of the securities settlement instruction query criteria by using the following two block elements:
This block element is mandatory and non-repetitive. It defines the type of query and whether the expected query response is related to an Instruction, Status or Status Period query.
This block element is mandatory and non-repetitive. It defines the criteria to extract the securities settlement instruction information.
The Securities Settlement Transaction Query message covers the following T2S message usages:

This query type enables the sender to query for information on the details of specific securities settlement instructions by specifying the pertinent criteria allowed from the list of business attributes within [Search Criteria] block element.
To query for securities settlement instruction information, the element [Query Type] must be filled with the code “INST” [Instruction].
Search Criteria Status may be present (optional) when using this query type.
Settlement Instruction Current Status Query (corresponding query type – ‘Status [STTS]’)

This query type enables the sender to query for information on the details of specific securities settlement instructions satisfying the defined combination of current business processing statuses by specifying:
Status Type (e.g. matching status, settlement status).
Status value (e.g. matched or unmatched for matching status and pending or failing for settlement status).
All securities settlement instructions satisfying the provided criteria and with a current status matching the status criteria provided are returned.
To query a securities settlement instruction current status query the element [Query Type] must be filled with the code “STTS” [Status].
Search Criteria Status/Type must be present (mandatory) when using this query type.
Settlement Instruction Status Audit Trail Query (corresponding query type – ‘Status Period [STPD]’)
This query type enables the sender to query for information on the details of specific settlement instructions satisfying specific statuses for a given period.
To query a settlement instruction status audit trail query the element [Query Type] must be filled with the code “STPD” [Status Period].
Search Criteria Status/Type and Status/DatePeriod must be present (mandatory) when using this query type.
All instructions satisfying the provided criteria and with the status matching the status criteria during the specified period provided are returned.

In response to the Securities Settlement Transaction Query message, T2S sends a Securities Settlement Transaction Query Response message (semt.027) with the corresponding requested securities settlement instructions based on the criteria as defined within the query message.
The Securities Settlement Transaction Query Response message is sent by T2S to a Central Securities Depository or a directly connected T2S participant (e.g. payment bank/settlement bank).
This message is used to provide information on securities settlement instructions, as selected in the search criteria defined in the query message (semt.026).
The Securities Settlement Transaction Query Response is composed of the following message building blocks:
This block element is mandatory and non-repetitive. It contains information about pagination of the report.
This block element is mandatory and non-repetitive. It contains general characteristics related to the report information.
This block element is optional and repetitive. It contains the specific transactions corresponding to the criteria of the query.
The Securities Settlement Transaction Query Response message covers the following T2S message usages:
Settlement Instruction Query Response (corresponding query type – ‘Instruction [INST]’)
This message usage provides details regarding the securities settlement instructions satisfying the query criteria of the corresponding settlement instruction query message.
To indicate a settlement instruction query response the element [Query Type] within the block element [Report General Details] is filled with the code “INST” [Instruction].
The element [Status And Reason] within the block element [Transactions] must not be present when using this query type.
Settlement Instruction Current Status Query Response (corresponding query type – ‘Status [STTS]’)
This message usage provides details regarding the securities settlement instructions satisfying the query criteria of the corresponding settlement instruction current status query message.
To indicate a settlement instruction current status query response the element [Query Type] within the block element [Report General Details] is filled with the code “STTS” [Status].
The element [Status And Reason] within the block element [Transactions] is present when using this query type.
Settlement Instruction Status Audit Trail Query Response (corresponding query type – ‘Status Period [STPD]’)
This message usage provides details regarding the securities settlement instructions satisfying the query criteria of the corresponding settlement instruction status audit trail query message.
To indicate a settlement instruction status audit trail query response the element [Query Type] within the block element [Report General Details] is filled with the code “STPD” [Status Period].
The element [Status And Reason] within the block element [Transactions] is present when using this query type.
The Securities Account Position Response message is sent by T2S to a CSD or any party authorised by them as response for the Securities Account Position Query message.
The Securities Account Position Response provides information about the different securities positions of a T2S Actor’s securities account(s) in T2S.
Depending on the search criteria of the Query, the response provides:
The position at a specific time of the current day.
The closing position for a specific day in the past.
The closing positions for a period of days in the past.
The Securities Account Position Response message is composed of the following message building blocks:
This building block is mandatory and non-repetitive. It defines the pagination of the message.

This building blocks is mandatory and non-repetitive. It specifies general information related to response such as the query reference, the activity or whether the data is either historical or current.
This block is optional and non-repetitive. It identifies the party who owns the account.

This block is optional and identifies the party that manages the account on behalf of the account owner, i.e. manages the registration and booking of entries on the account, calculates balances on the account and provides information about the account.
This building block is optional and repetitive. This block provides the net position of a segregated holding, in a single security, within the overall position held in a set of securities accounts.
The Securities Transaction Penalties Report message definition is specifically designed to support the technical functions depending on the following message usages:

Daily cash penalty list Report. This report is sent to actors to inform about the cash penalties computed for a given business day. In case of a CSD, the information shall include the cash penalties that are either imposed or credited to all of its participants. In case the actor is a CSD participant, the information shall include the cash penalties that are either imposed or credited to the CSD participant itself.

List of modified penalties. This report is sent to actors to inform about the modifications made in existing cash penalties that have occurred since the previous recalculation process. The possible modifications that may occur in a penalty, and hence reported in the List of Modified Penalties, are: whether a cash penalty has been removed, re-included, re-allocated or switched by a CSD or whether a cash penalty has been automatically updated after the recalculation of the penalty triggered by a change in the relevant reference data like the valuation of a certain ISIN or the penalty rate to be applied.

Monthly report of aggregated amounts of cash penalties. This report is sent to actors to inform about the aggregated amounts of the cash penalties computed for the business days of the previous month. Monthly report of aggregated amounts of cash penalties considers the last available value of the amount of each of the cash penalties to be aggregated, considering all the modifications performed on the cash penalties.
The Securities Transaction Penalties Report message is composed of the following message building blocks:

This building block is mandatory (the pagination of the report is only allowed when agreed between the parties) and non-repetitive. It contains information about pagination of the report: Page number and Last Page Indicator.
This building block is mandatory and non-repetitive. It contains general characteristics related to the report information.

This block is mandatory and non-repetitive. It identifies the party that manages the account on behalf of the account owner, i.e. manages the registration and booking of entries on the account, calculates balances on the account and provides information about the account.
This block is optional (provided Activity Indicator is TRUE) and repetitive. It contains detailed information related to the computed penalties.

A BusinessRole represents an entity (or a class of entities) of the real world, physical or legal, a person, a group of persons, a corporation. Examples of BusinessRoles: “Financial Institution”, “Automated Clearing House”, “Central Securities Depository”.

A Participant is a functional role performed by a BusinessRole in a particular BusinessProcess or BusinessTransaction. Examples of Participants: the “user” of a system, “debtor”, “creditor”, “investor”.

The relationship between BusinessRoles and Participants is many-to-many. One BusinessRole can be involved as different Participants at different moments in time or at the same time. Examples of BusinessRoles:  "user", "debtor”, "creditor", "investor". Different BusinessRoles can be involved as the same Participant.

In the context of a Business Transaction, the process enables the reconciliation of (pending and posted) transactions and their computed penalties (if any) by providing the associated data. The main processes are highlighted in green, the surrounding processes in blue.
The reconciliation communication flows can be represented as follows:

The Securities Account Position Query message returns the latest securities position at the given time of the day that the query has been requested for the specified securities accounts. In case the T2S Actor requests for a Securities Account Position History Query, he should indicate either the securities account or the account owner as search criteria. In a Securities Account Position History Query, T2S returns all closing securities positions on the dates within the specified time period for the specified securities accounts. In response to the Securities Account Position Query message, T2S sends a semt.040 message with the list of the different securities positions of a T2S Actor's securities account or a sese.022 message in case of error.

The Securities Settlement Transaction Query message is sent by a Central Securities Depository or a directly connected T2S participant (e.g. payment bank/settlement bank) to T2S. This message is used to request information on Settlement Instructions.
This message is sent to T2S for the following query types:
Settlement Instruction Status Audit Trail Query.

In response to the Securities Settlement Transaction Query message, T2S sends a Securities Settlement Transaction Query Response message (semt.027) with the corresponding requested settlement instructions or a Securities Status Or Statement Query Status Advice message (sese.022) in the case of a business error.

The Securities Settlement Transaction Query Response message is sent by T2S to a Central Securities Depository or a directly connected T2S participant (e.g. payment bank/settlement bank). This message is used to provide information on Settlement Instructions based on the criteria as defined within the query message.

To request the Securities Settlement Transaction Query Response message, the sender sends a semt.026 message containing search criteria to restrict the query. This message is sent by T2S in the following message usages:
Settlement Instruction Current Status Query Response.
Settlement Instruction Status Audit Trail Query Response.

The Securities Account Position Response message is sent by T2S to a CSD, or any party authorised by them, as response for the semt.025 message. The Securities Account Position Response provides information about the different securities positions of a T2S Actor’s securities account in T2S.

The Securities Transaction Penalties Report message is sent by T2S to T2S Actors, i.e. CSDs or CSD participants, to provide them with the Daily Penalty List, the List of Modified Penalties and the Monthly Aggregated Amounts of penalties for the previous month. T2S shall allow the relevant T2S Actor to receive penalties information under its default data scope.
In case of a CSD, the information shall include the penalties that are either imposed or credited to all the parties belonging to the CSD data scope.
In case of a CSD participant (or an External CSD), the information shall include the penalties that are either imposed or credited to the CSD participant (or the External CSD).

The T2S operator is the top level of the hierarchical role and access rights model. The T2S operator role classification includes all T2S system users of the entity, which will be responsible for the day-to-day operation and management of T2S. The T2S actors managed by this entity shall be CSDs and NCBs participating in T2S. At the highest level, the T2S operator shall have access to all data and functionality in the subordinate level.

The process provides responses to queries regarding Settlement instructions previously sent, Securities Account Balances and Penalties computed due to Settlement failures and allows the sending of reconciliation results via query responses or via reporting.
The process is triggered either by the system through a scheduled event in case of reports or by the receipt of a query request sent by the Instructing Party.

The respective business object (i.e settlement Instructions, Securities Accounts, Penalties computed) must exist to query within the scope of the Instructing Party and which correspond to the criteria as defined within the query and report.
The Instructing Party must hold necessary privileges within the Static Data configuration to receive reports.

records.text: This Message Definition Report covers a set of five MessageDefinitions developed by Banco de España and Banque de France on behalf of 4CB in close collaboration with SWIFT, submitted by Deutsche Bundesbank on behalf of 4CB and approved by Securities Standards Evaluation Groups (SEG) on 19 February 2026.

Originally, these messages have been designed to support the T2S community with retrieving securities settlement and securities position related information from the platform. T2S (TARGET2-Securities) is a European securities settlement engine which offers centralised settlement in central bank money across all European securities markets. The fundamental objective of T2S is to integrate and harmonise the highly fragmented securities settlement infrastructure in Europe. It aims to reduce the costs of cross-border securities settlement and increase competition and choice among providers of post-trading services in Europe.
The detailed description of each MessageDefinition is provided in Message Definition Report Part 2.

records.text: The Securities Transaction Penalties report message is specifically designed to support the provision of information to T2S actors related to the cash penalties computed by T2S that are either imposed or credited to those actors or their participants. On a daily basis, T2S shall compute cash penalties for settlement instructions which have not been settled after their intended settlement date.

Additionally, this message also supports the reporting of cash penalties that have been modified since its first calculation in T2S by a CSD or recalculated by T2S due to several circumstances like changes in the penalty rates to be applied or the valuation of the ISIN of the settlement instructions related to the penalty.

These messages are to be used with the ISO 20022 Business Application Header (head.001). The schema and more information about the Business Application Header (BAH) can be found on the www.iso20022.org web site
Settlement Queries Responses Reports message set consists of:
This section provides for an overview of the functionality of each message in the scope of this submission, See Message Definition Report Part 2 for the message definitions and formats.
The Settlement Queries Responses and Report message definitions are specifically designed to support the following technical functions:

The Securities Account Position Query provides CSDs and T2S participants with the functionality to query for the latest or historical data on balances in the Securities Accounts with multiple criteria and, in some cases, satisfying multiple values or range of values.
The Securities Account Position Query message is composed of the following message building blocks.
This building block is mandatory and defines the criteria used to report on the securities account position allowing to choose for the latest or historical data.
This building block is mandatory and provides the criteria to extract the securities account position result set.

In response to the Securities Account Position Query T2S sends a Securities Account Position Response message (semt.040) with the corresponding Securities Account position details matching the criteria as defined within the query.

The Securities Settlement Transaction Query message is sent by a Central Securities Depository or a Directly Connected T2S Participant (e.g. payment bank/settlement bank) to T2S to query for information on securities settlement instructions with multiple criteria and, in some cases, satisfying multiple values or range of values.
This message is composed of the following message building block:
This building block is mandatory and non-repetitive. It contains the definition of the securities settlement instruction query criteria by using the following two block elements:
This block element is mandatory and non-repetitive. It defines the type of query and whether the expected query response is related to an Instruction, Status or Status Period query.
This block element is mandatory and non-repetitive. It defines the criteria to extract the securities settlement instruction information.
The Securities Settlement Transaction Query message covers the following T2S message usages:

This query type enables the sender to query for information on the details of specific securities settlement instructions by specifying the pertinent criteria allowed from the list of business attributes within [Search Criteria] block element.
To query for securities settlement instruction information, the element [Query Type] must be filled with the code “INST” [Instruction].
Search Criteria Status may be present (optional) when using this query type.
Settlement Instruction Current Status Query (corresponding query type – ‘Status [STTS]’)

This query type enables the sender to query for information on the details of specific securities settlement instructions satisfying the defined combination of current business processing statuses by specifying:
Status Type (e.g. matching status, settlement status).
Status value (e.g. matched or unmatched for matching status and pending or failing for settlement status).
All securities settlement instructions satisfying the provided criteria and with a current status matching the status criteria provided are returned.
To query a securities settlement instruction current status query the element [Query Type] must be filled with the code “STTS” [Status].
Search Criteria Status/Type must be present (mandatory) when using this query type.
Settlement Instruction Status Audit Trail Query (corresponding query type – ‘Status Period [STPD]’)
This query type enables the sender to query for information on the details of specific settlement instructions satisfying specific statuses for a given period.
To query a settlement instruction status audit trail query the element [Query Type] must be filled with the code “STPD” [Status Period].
Search Criteria Status/Type and Status/DatePeriod must be present (mandatory) when using this query type.
All instructions satisfying the provided criteria and with the status matching the status criteria during the specified period provided are returned.

In response to the Securities Settlement Transaction Query message, T2S sends a Securities Settlement Transaction Query Response message (semt.027) with the corresponding requested securities settlement instructions based on the criteria as defined within the query message.
The Securities Settlement Transaction Query Response message is sent by T2S to a Central Securities Depository or a directly connected T2S participant (e.g. payment bank/settlement bank).
This message is used to provide information on securities settlement instructions, as selected in the search criteria defined in the query message (semt.026).
The Securities Settlement Transaction Query Response is composed of the following message building blocks:
This block element is mandatory and non-repetitive. It contains information about pagination of the report.
This block element is mandatory and non-repetitive. It contains general characteristics related to the report information.
This block element is optional and repetitive. It contains the specific transactions corresponding to the criteria of the query.
The Securities Settlement Transaction Query Response message covers the following T2S message usages:
Settlement Instruction Query Response (corresponding query type – ‘Instruction [INST]’)
This message usage provides details regarding the securities settlement instructions satisfying the query criteria of the corresponding settlement instruction query message.
To indicate a settlement instruction query response the element [Query Type] within the block element [Report General Details] is filled with the code “INST” [Instruction].
The element [Status And Reason] within the block element [Transactions] must not be present when using this query type.
Settlement Instruction Current Status Query Response (corresponding query type – ‘Status [STTS]’)
This message usage provides details regarding the securities settlement instructions satisfying the query criteria of the corresponding settlement instruction current status query message.
To indicate a settlement instruction current status query response the element [Query Type] within the block element [Report General Details] is filled with the code “STTS” [Status].
The element [Status And Reason] within the block element [Transactions] is present when using this query type.
Settlement Instruction Status Audit Trail Query Response (corresponding query type – ‘Status Period [STPD]’)
This message usage provides details regarding the securities settlement instructions satisfying the query criteria of the corresponding settlement instruction status audit trail query message.
To indicate a settlement instruction status audit trail query response the element [Query Type] within the block element [Report General Details] is filled with the code “STPD” [Status Period].
The element [Status And Reason] within the block element [Transactions] is present when using this query type.
The Securities Account Position Response message is sent by T2S to a CSD or any party authorised by them as response for the Securities Account Position Query message.
The Securities Account Position Response provides information about the different securities positions of a T2S Actor’s securities account(s) in T2S.
Depending on the search criteria of the Query, the response provides:
The position at a specific time of the current day.
The closing position for a specific day in the past.
The closing positions for a period of days in the past.
The Securities Account Position Response message is composed of the following message building blocks:
This building block is mandatory and non-repetitive. It defines the pagination of the message.

This building blocks is mandatory and non-repetitive. It specifies general information related to response such as the query reference, the activity or whether the data is either historical or current.
This block is optional and non-repetitive. It identifies the party who owns the account.

This block is optional and identifies the party that manages the account on behalf of the account owner, i.e. manages the registration and booking of entries on the account, calculates balances on the account and provides information about the account.
This building block is optional and repetitive. This block provides the net position of a segregated holding, in a single security, within the overall position held in a set of securities accounts.
The Securities Transaction Penalties Report message definition is specifically designed to support the technical functions depending on the following message usages:

Daily cash penalty list Report. This report is sent to actors to inform about the cash penalties computed for a given business day. In case of a CSD, the information shall include the cash penalties that are either imposed or credited to all of its participants. In case the actor is a CSD participant, the information shall include the cash penalties that are either imposed or credited to the CSD participant itself.

List of modified penalties. This report is sent to actors to inform about the modifications made in existing cash penalties that have occurred since the previous recalculation process. The possible modifications that may occur in a penalty, and hence reported in the List of Modified Penalties, are: whether a cash penalty has been removed, re-included, re-allocated or switched by a CSD or whether a cash penalty has been automatically updated after the recalculation of the penalty triggered by a change in the relevant reference data like the valuation of a certain ISIN or the penalty rate to be applied.

Monthly report of aggregated amounts of cash penalties. This report is sent to actors to inform about the aggregated amounts of the cash penalties computed for the business days of the previous month. Monthly report of aggregated amounts of cash penalties considers the last available value of the amount of each of the cash penalties to be aggregated, considering all the modifications performed on the cash penalties.
The Securities Transaction Penalties Report message is composed of the following message building blocks:

This building block is mandatory (the pagination of the report is only allowed when agreed between the parties) and non-repetitive. It contains information about pagination of the report: Page number and Last Page Indicator.
This building block is mandatory and non-repetitive. It contains general characteristics related to the report information.

This block is mandatory and non-repetitive. It identifies the party that manages the account on behalf of the account owner, i.e. manages the registration and booking of entries on the account, calculates balances on the account and provides information about the account.
This block is optional (provided Activity Indicator is TRUE) and repetitive. It contains detailed information related to the computed penalties.

A BusinessRole represents an entity (or a class of entities) of the real world, physical or legal, a person, a group of persons, a corporation. Examples of BusinessRoles: “Financial Institution”, “Automated Clearing House”, “Central Securities Depository”.

A Participant is a functional role performed by a BusinessRole in a particular BusinessProcess or BusinessTransaction. Examples of Participants: the “user” of a system, “debtor”, “creditor”, “investor”.

The relationship between BusinessRoles and Participants is many-to-many. One BusinessRole can be involved as different Participants at different moments in time or at the same time. Examples of BusinessRoles:  "user", "debtor”, "creditor", "investor". Different BusinessRoles can be involved as the same Participant.

records.text: The Securities Account Position Query message returns the latest securities position at the given time of the day that the query has been requested for the specified securities accounts. In case the T2S Actor requests for a Securities Account Position History Query, he should indicate either the securities account or the account owner as search criteria. In a Securities Account Position History Query, T2S returns all closing securities positions on the dates within the specified time period for the specified securities accounts. In response to the Securities Account Position Query message, T2S sends a semt.040 message with the list of the different securities positions of a T2S Actor's securities account or a sese.022 message in case of error.

The Securities Settlement Transaction Query message is sent by a Central Securities Depository or a directly connected T2S participant (e.g. payment bank/settlement bank) to T2S. This message is used to request information on Settlement Instructions.
This message is sent to T2S for the following query types:
Settlement Instruction Status Audit Trail Query.

In response to the Securities Settlement Transaction Query message, T2S sends a Securities Settlement Transaction Query Response message (semt.027) with the corresponding requested settlement instructions or a Securities Status Or Statement Query Status Advice message (sese.022) in the case of a business error.

The Securities Settlement Transaction Query Response message is sent by T2S to a Central Securities Depository or a directly connected T2S participant (e.g. payment bank/settlement bank). This message is used to provide information on Settlement Instructions based on the criteria as defined within the query message.

To request the Securities Settlement Transaction Query Response message, the sender sends a semt.026 message containing search criteria to restrict the query. This message is sent by T2S in the following message usages:
Settlement Instruction Current Status Query Response.
Settlement Instruction Status Audit Trail Query Response.

The Securities Account Position Response message is sent by T2S to a CSD, or any party authorised by them, as response for the semt.025 message. The Securities Account Position Response provides information about the different securities positions of a T2S Actor’s securities account in T2S.

The Securities Transaction Penalties Report message is sent by T2S to T2S Actors, i.e. CSDs or CSD participants, to provide them with the Daily Penalty List, the List of Modified Penalties and the Monthly Aggregated Amounts of penalties for the previous month. T2S shall allow the relevant T2S Actor to receive penalties information under its default data scope.
In case of a CSD, the information shall include the penalties that are either imposed or credited to all the parties belonging to the CSD data scope.
In case of a CSD participant (or an External CSD), the information shall include the penalties that are either imposed or credited to the CSD participant (or the External CSD).
